full_judgment: 9. Mr. S.R. Pal has relied on (1950) A.C. 458, AIR 1965 (SC) 87, 6 DLR 634, AIR 1956 (SC). 415, and PLD 1963 (Da), 595, The Privy Council case, that is the first mentioned one, is the basis of the decisions in the other cases as referred to and as such this should be discussed first. It is Sambasivam vs. Public Prosecutor, Federation of Malaya. Facts in brief of that case are that Sambasivam, appellant, was travelling on foot along with two Chinese. They met a party of three Malayas with whom a sudden fight broke out in the course of which one Chinese was killed. So far as the appellant is concerned, it was alleged that he had with him a revolver which he held out and pointed at one of the Malayas, He was charged with carrying a firearm and also being in possession of ten rounds of ammunition. He was acquitted of the charge of being in possession ammunition but be was convicted on the charge of carrying a loaded firearm and this conviction led to the appeal before the Privy Council. Their Lordships allowed the appeal and acquitted the appellant on the ground that the evidence regarding the appellant carrying a loaded firearm was inadmissible in law as in his trial for possessing ammunition the evidence about possession of ammunition was rejected.
